pages.h2: Is each person better prepared than a year ago?
pages.label: Full article

post:
After fifteen articles on regenerative management, I realised I had never answered the simplest question: what is it?

My definition is short. Regenerative management prepares managers and their teams for today's challenges by valuing their past experience, acknowledging their present concerns and preparing them for their future.

In practice, it starts with a concrete question: what is draining people at work without creating any value? Pointless meetings, absurd reporting and endless sign-offs come off the list first.

It also changes how a manager judges a year. An extractive manager counts what he has obtained. A regenerative manager asks whether each person on the team is more capable, more confident and better prepared for the future.

Regenerative leadership is the theoretical umbrella. Regenerative management is pulling on your boots and starting to dig.
